body.en: Tragedy on the Nepal-Tibet border. Plus: How Mark Carney stood up to Trump • Get the Guardian Weekly delivered to your home address Over the last week, the world has watched with horror the scenes from the Tibet-Nepal border where a devastating torrent of mud, water and ice tore along the Bhotekoshi River, destroying entire communities and leaving more than 1,000 people dead and several thousand more missing. From the Nepali town of Devighat, our south Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis-Petersen describes a nightmarish scene of overflowing mortuaries and unidentifiable bodies, as shellshocked survivors of the flood slowly return to the ruins of their homes. Continue reading...
body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏边境发生的悲剧。另外：马克·卡尼如何对抗特朗普 • 将《卫报》周刊送到你的家庭住址 上周，全世界都惊恐地目睹了西藏和尼泊尔边境的景象，一场毁灭性的泥浆、水和冰沿着博特科希河冲刷，摧毁了整个社区，造成 1,000 多人死亡，数千人失踪。我们的南亚记者汉娜·埃利斯-彼得森在尼泊尔德维加特镇描述了一个噩梦般的场景，停尸间已经满溢，尸体无法辨认，洪水中遭受炮弹袭击的幸存者正在慢慢返回家园的废墟。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The Bhotekoshi River's devastating flood on the Nepal-Tibet border has brought unimaginable loss, with over a thousand dead and thousands more missing. In the face of such profound grief and destruction, we hold onto the hope of a future where all tears are wiped away and suffering ceases. May Yahweh comfort those who mourn and guide efforts toward healing...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏边境博特科西河的毁灭性洪水带来了难以想象的损失，造成一千多人死亡，数千人失踪。面对如此深切的悲痛和毁灭，我们紧握着对未来的希望，那是一个所有眼泪都被擦干、痛苦将停止的未来。愿雅伟安慰那些哀恸的人，并指引疗愈和重建的努力。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: The shifting ties in Australia's backyard as 'deep pockets' beckon
title.zh: 澳大利亚后院的变动关系：‘深口袋’的诱惑

summary.en: While China stirs tensions over Taiwan in Palau, island leaders are urging Canberra to focus on climate and drug crime.
summary.zh: 在中国试图在帕劳挑起关于台湾的紧张局势之际，岛屿领导人正敦促堪培拉关注气候变化和毒品犯罪。

body.en:
China and Taiwan's diplomatic tug-of-war is casting a shadow over the ongoing Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) as a handful of national leaders declined to attend — however, experts on the ground caution that a geopolitical focus risks ignoring the core priorities of Australia's neighbours.

The annual 18-member gathering in the Taiwanese-allied nation of Palau opened on Monday with climate change, economic security, and the rising influence of the transnational drug trade top of the agenda.

China has said it has "serious concerns" that Taiwan was invited to attend in its own right, while questions have been raised about whether China has influenced five of 18 national leaders from the forum (those of Kiribati, Fiji, Vanuatu, Samoa and Solomon Island) not to attend.

The cornerstone regional political forum began this year with a pointed message from Palau's President Surangel Whipps Jr, who urged nations to adhere to this year's theme of unity and reminded outside partners that they "do not choose our destination".

This year's PIF takes place as Kiribati moves to constitutionally restrict diplomatic recognition to UN member states only — thus excluding Taiwan — while China actively seeks to strip Taiwan of its 'development partner' status in the forum. This comes nearly two months after a Chinese ballistic missile test in the Pacific Ocean .

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Taiwan, a self-governing democracy, broke away from mainland China in 1949. China views it as Chinese territory that must be brought under its control by force if necessary.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has made strengthening regional ties a key focus of his administration's foreign policy, signing multiple bilateral agreements with countries like Fiji, Vanuatu, and Tuvalu.

But despite the noise around China, "leaders have made it clear they're here to work" Tess Newton Cain, principal consultant at Asia-Pacific strategic firm Sustineo, told SBS News from Koror.

"The issue of the China-Taiwan tussle is largely a distraction, and one that they try to minimise."

On Wednesday, $600 million in Australian funding was announced to tackle transnational drug smuggling from South America that is increasingly causing harm across the Pacific.

China has made the PIF something of a battleground, maintaining that Taiwan ought to be sidelined during talks, as it is not technically a "dialogue partner" due to a difficult compromise that PIF members have reached over its status for the past three decades.

Palau, one of the few nations that maintains official diplomatic ties with Taiwan, has accused China of running a coercion campaign against it after travel...
body.zh: 由于少数国家领导人拒绝出席，中国和台湾的外交拉锯战给正在进行的太平洋岛屿论坛（PIF）蒙上了阴影。然而，现场专家警告称，地缘政治焦点可能会忽视澳大利亚邻国的核心优先事项。 一年一度的 18 名成员聚会于周一在台湾盟友帕劳开幕，气候变化、经济安全和跨国毒品贸易影响力不断上升成为首要议题。 中国表示，它“严重关切”台湾本身受邀参加，同时也有人质疑中国是否影响论坛 18 个国家领导人中的 5 个（基里巴斯、斐济、瓦努阿图、萨摩亚和所罗门群岛）不参加。 这一基石区域政治论坛于今年拉开帷幕，帕劳总统小苏兰吉尔·惠普斯发出了尖锐的信息，他敦促各国坚持今年的团结主题，并提醒外部伙伴“我们的目的地不是他们选择的”。 今年的PIF召开之际，基里巴斯从宪法上采取行动，限制仅对联合国成员国进行外交承认，从而将台湾排除在外，而中国则积极寻求剥夺台湾在论坛中的“发展伙伴”地位。这是中国在太平洋进行弹道导弹试验近两个月后的事。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 台湾是一个自治民主国家，于 1949 年脱离中国大陆。中国将其视为中国领土，必要时必须使用武力将其置于其控制之下。 安东尼·阿尔巴内塞总理将加强区域关系作为其政府外交政策的重点，与斐济、瓦努阿图和图瓦卢等国签署了多项双边协议。 不过，尽管中国周围一片喧嚣，“领导人已经明确表示，他们来这里是为了工作”，亚太战略公司 Sustineo 的首席顾问泰丝·牛顿·凯恩 (Tess Newton Cain) 在科罗尔告诉 SBS 新闻。 “中国与台湾的争斗问题在很大程度上是一种干扰，他们试图将其最小化。” 周三，澳大利亚宣布提供 6 亿美元资金，用于打击来自南美洲的跨国毒品走私，这种走私在太平洋沿岸造成的危害日益严重。 中国已将太平洋岛礁论坛变成了一个战场，坚持认为台湾应该在谈判中靠边站，因为过去三十年来，太平洋岛礁论坛成员就其地位达成了艰难的妥协，因此从技术上讲，台湾并不是“对话伙伴”。 帕劳是少数几个与台湾保持正式外交关系的国家之一，该国指责中国在旅行后对其进行胁迫行动......

reflection.en: The leaders of Pacific island nations are navigating complex geopolitical currents, yet their urgent pleas to Australia highlight their immediate concerns: climate change and the drug trade. These are matters of justice and well-being for their people, echoing the prophet Micah's call to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with Yahweh. Their focus on...
reflection.zh: 太平洋岛国领导人正驾驭复杂的地缘政治暗流，但他们向澳大利亚发出的紧急呼吁，凸显了他们眼前的关切：气候变化和毒品交易。这些关乎其人民的福祉和公义，呼应了先知弥迦的呼召，要行公义、好怜悯、谦卑地与雅伟同行。他们关注切实的需要而非遥远的冲突，提醒我们真正的优先事项往往在哪里。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: As glaciers melt, can communities be protected?
title.zh: 冰川融化，社区能否得到保护？

summary.en: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.
summary.zh: 气温上升增加了山区洪水和雪崩的风险。尼泊尔和西藏的灾难表明迫切需要解决方案，以及可能有助于挽救生命的工具。

body.en:
Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

High mountain glaciers formed in the ice age are retreating and becoming unstable as the burning of fossil fuels heats the climate and leads to a decline in snowfall.

The instability creates the conditions for large glacial sections to collapse, triggering ice and rock avalanches that can dam river valleys before tidal waves of water are released.

Following the glacier collapse that triggered what is known as a mountain tsunami in Nepal and Tibet on August 26 , thousands are still missing and feared dead. Unlike the 2025 glacier avalanche that destroyed the town of Blatten in Switzerland — where nearly all inhabitants were evacuated — a lack of early warning systems in the Himalayas left locals and tourists at the mercy of flash floods .

The causes of glacier collapse are part of a complex web of interrelated changes to high mountain landscapes due in part to rising global temperatures, say scientists.

Levan Tielidze, research fellow in glacial geomorphology at Australia's Monash University, said the Himalayas are not, as is often imagined, a "frozen and relatively stable environment," but "dynamic systems in which glaciers , snow, permafrost, rock slopes, rivers and monsoon processes interact." 

"As the climate warms, these components are changing simultaneously, meaning hazards can cascade from one process into another," he told DW. When rock, ice and water interact in more unpredictable ways on the world's highest peaks, the resulting debris flows "can transform into a catastrophic flood far downstream."

Almost 25 years ago, in what was then the biggest glacial collapse in history, one glacier crashed onto another in the Caucasus Mountains of North Ossetia in Russia. The event caused avalanches of ice and debris that slid more than 24 kilometers (15 miles) and killed around 125 people.

"The Kolka Glacier disaster was one of the early warnings of the increasing occurrence and potential severity of such glacier-related hazards," said Tielidze. 

Meanwhile, the UN says glaciers in Nepalese mountains have declined by one-third in 30 years, which has added to their instability. 

Some research suggests that even if emissions from burning fossil fuels were low enough to prevent the planet from heating by more than 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 Fahrenheit) compared to pre-industrial times, the wider Hindu Kush Himalayan region could lose up to half its glacier cover — compared to 2020 levels — by the end of the century.

For Dipesh Chapagain, senior scientist at...
body.zh: 气温上升增加了山区发生洪水和雪崩的风险。尼泊尔和西藏的灾难表明迫切需要解决方案以及可以帮助拯救生命的工具。 由于化石燃料的燃烧导致气候变暖并导致降雪量减少，冰河时代形成的高山冰川正在后退并变得不稳定。这种不稳定性为大片冰川崩塌创造了条件，引发冰雪崩塌，在潮水释放之前可能会堵塞河谷。 8 月 26 日，冰川崩塌在尼泊尔和西藏引发了山地海啸，之后仍有数千人失踪并恐已死亡。与 2025 年摧毁瑞士巴滕镇的冰川雪崩不同，当时几乎所有居民都被疏散，喜马拉雅山缺乏预警系统，导致当地人和游客受到山洪爆发的影响。 科学家表示，冰川崩塌的原因是高山景观相互关联的复杂变化网络的一部分，部分原因是全球气温上升。 澳大利亚莫纳什大学冰川地貌学研究员 Levan Tielidze 表示，喜马拉雅山并不像人们通常想象的那样是一个“冰冻且相对稳定的环境”，而是“冰川、积雪、永久冻土、岩石斜坡、河流和季风过程相互作用的动态系统”。 他告诉德国之声：“随着气候变暖，这些组成部分同时发生变化，这意味着危害可能从一个过程级联到另一个过程。” 当岩石、冰和水在世界最高峰上以更难以预测的方式相互作用时，由此产生的泥石流“可能会在下游转化为灾难性的洪水”。 大约 25 年前，俄罗斯联邦北奥塞梯高加索山脉的一座冰川与另一座冰川相撞，发生了当时历史上最严重的冰川崩塌事件。该事件导致冰雪崩塌和碎片滑落超过 24 公里（15 英里），造成约 125 人死亡。 蒂利泽告诉德国之声：“科尔卡冰川灾难是此类冰川相关灾害日益频繁且潜在严重性的早期预警之一。” 与此同时，联合国表示，尼泊尔山区的冰川在 30 年内减少了三分之一，这加剧了冰川的不稳定。 一些研究表明，即使燃烧化石燃料的排放量足够低，足以防止地球升温超过工业化前时期 2 摄氏度（36 华氏度），与 2020 年的水平相比，更广泛的兴都库什喜马拉雅地区的冰川覆盖面积可能会减少多达一半……

reflection.en: The news from Nepal and Tibet paints a stark picture of creation groaning under the weight of climate change. Glaciers, formed over millennia, are becoming unstable, leading to devastating 'mountain tsunamis.' This echoes Romans 8:22, which speaks of all creation groaning in the pains of childbirth, awaiting its redemption from decay. The urgent need for...
reflection.zh: 来自尼泊尔和西藏的新闻描绘了一幅严峻的景象：在气候变化的重压下，受造界发出痛苦的呻吟。历经千年形成的冰川正变得不稳定，导致毁灭性的“山洪海啸”。这呼应了罗马书8:22所说，万物都在一同叹息，劳苦直到如今，等待着从败坏中得释放。对解决方案的迫切需求，凸显了我们共同的责任，要关爱这个脆弱的世界。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Albanese responds after China warns of 'consequences' over Taiwan at Pacific summit
title.zh: 中国警告台湾出席太平洋岛国论坛将带来“后果”

summary.en: China's top diplomat for Pacific Island Countries, Qian Bo, has warned of 'consequences' regarding Taiwan's presence as a development partner at the annual Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) leaders' meeting in Palau. He expressed China's 'serious concerns' and called Taiwan's participation 'inappropriate,' though he denied...
summary.zh: 中国太平洋岛国事务特使钱波警告，台湾作为太平洋岛国论坛（PIF）年度领导人会议的发展伙伴出席将带来“后果”。他表达了中国“严重关切”，并称台湾的参与“不恰当”，但他否认其言论是威胁。

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has stopped short of criticising China over threats of "consequences" for Taiwan's attendance at an annual Pacific summit, saying the forum decides who takes part.

Albanese's comments follow a warning from China's top Pacific Islands diplomat, who said "there will always be consequences" for Taiwan's strong presence at the annual Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) leaders' meeting in Palau, with the highly charged three-day talks officially starting on Tuesday.

Albanese said he was "not distracted" when asked if Taiwan's presence was a distraction. Asked if he thought it was appropriate for China to make threats, the prime minister said: "The Pacific Islands Forum determines what happens here, not any other country."

Earlier, China's special envoy for Pacific Island affairs, Qian Bo, denied his comments were a threat, but said China has "serious concerns" about Taiwan's status as a development partner at the forum.

"There will always be consequences. You know, this is objected to by all, so this should not have happened. We think it's very inappropriate to do so," he told Australian reporters while leaving the forum's opening ceremony on Monday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Taiwan, a self-governing democracy, broke away from mainland China in 1949. Beijing views it as Chinese territory that must be brought under its control by force if necessary .

Like the United States, Australia recognises and has formal ties with China, but maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan.

Neither China nor Taiwan are part of the 18-member group at the forum, but countries including the United States and China have traditionally been invited as dialogue partners. Taiwan has been categorised as a development partner since 1993 and is being represented this year by foreign minister Lin Chia-lung, along with a sizeable delegation.

Palau is one of only three Pacific nations to have diplomatic relations with Taiwan, which has created great friction between the hosts and China over the past decade. In 2017, China placed de facto "tourist bans" on the tiny Micronesian country, which received 40 per cent of its GDP from the tourism industry, in an apparent attempt to sway Palau's diplomatic position away from Taiwan.

Palau's president Surangel Whipps Jr said on Sunday he was aware there would be "threats" of retaliation if Taiwan attended this year's talks.

"Let's not use this as a place that we should be threatening or making people feel uncomfortable," he told reporters.

"China doesn't tell us that we cannot be a partner to Taiwan. That is our sovereign decision, not their decision."

body.zh: 中国太平洋岛国最高外交官警告说，台湾在帕劳举行的太平洋岛国论坛（PIF）年度领导人会议上的强势参与“总会产生后果”，拉开了周二正式开始的为期三天的高度紧张的会谈。 北京太平洋岛国事务特使钱波否认他的言论构成威胁，但表示中国对台湾在论坛上作为发展伙伴的地位“严重关切”。 “总会有后果的。你知道，这是所有人都反对的，所以这不应该发生。我们认为这样做是非常不合适的，”他在周一离开开幕式时告诉澳大利亚记者。 中国和台湾都不属于该论坛的 18 个成员国，但美国和中国等国家历来被邀请作为对话伙伴。台湾自1993年起就被列为发展伙伴，今年由外交部长林家龙率领一个规模庞大的代表团出席。 帕劳是仅有的三个与台湾建交的太平洋国家之一，过去十年来，东道主与中国之间产生了巨大摩擦。 2017年，北京对这个密克罗尼西亚小国实施了事实上的“旅游禁令”，该国GDP的40%来自旅游业，显然是试图动摇帕劳的外交立场，使其远离台北。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 帕劳总统小苏兰吉尔·惠普斯周日表示，他知道如果台湾参加今年的会谈，将会有“报复威胁”。 他对记者说：“我们不要把这里当作我们应该威胁或让人们感到不舒服的地方。” “中国没有告诉我们，我们不能成为台湾的合作伙伴。这是我们的主权决定，而不是他们的决定。” 钱其琛还声称，中国得到了PIF“大多数”成员国的“理解和支持”，并向帕劳“非常明确”地表明了自己的立场。 今年的PIF在正式开始前就陷入了争议，六位领导人被确认缺席，其中包括即将离任的论坛主席、所罗门群岛总理马修·韦尔，以及基里巴斯亲北京总统塔内蒂·马毛，后者特意派了前驻华大使大卫·蒂博代替。 他们缺席的原因包括国家议会职责和健康问题，威尔士已抵达科罗尔，并被迫在周末返回家乡，以应对可能的领导挑战。但缺席的关键领导人让人怀疑，在为期三天的活动中，是否可以就关键议程项目（包括气候行动）采取有意义的集体行动……

reflection.en: As leaders gather in Palau for the Pacific Islands Forum, diplomatic tensions simmer. China's envoy has voiced strong objections to Taiwan's participation, warning of 'consequences.' In such moments of heightened political friction, the call to pursue peace and seek diplomatic solutions, even amidst disagreement, remains paramount.
reflection.zh: 在太平洋岛国论坛领导人在帕劳举行会议之际，外交紧张局势悄然升温。中国特使对台湾的参与表达了强烈反对，并警告将有“后果”。在政治摩擦加剧的时刻，即使存在分歧，寻求和平与外交解决方案的呼吁仍然至关重要。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: 'Hoping for a miracle': Family of missing Australian in Nepal speaks
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪灾死亡人数超950人，救援人员争分夺秒营救被困隧道工人

summary.en: Rescuers are urgently working to free hundreds of workers trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites that were inundated by mud from catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border. The combined death toll in Nepal and China has surpassed 950, with over 4400 people missing. At least 900 workers are unaccounted for at...
summary.zh: 在尼泊尔-中国边境发生灾难性洪水后，救援人员正争分夺秒地营救被埋在水电站隧道中的数百名工人。尼泊尔和中国的合计死亡人数已超过950人，另有超过4400人失踪。受洪水影响的12个水电项目至少有900名工人下落不明。

body.en:
The Australian government has confirmed two Australians have been safely located amid catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border as the number of people killed climbs and increasingly desperate families search for missing loved ones.

The combined deaths in Nepal and China surpassed 1,000, with more than 4,400 people — including 42 Australians — missing.

In a statement, his family said he had been visiting Mount Kailash on a pilgrimage trek when the floods hit. He went missing shortly after making contact at the Gyirong Port border crossing.

"Luke is an extremely strong, compassionate, disciplined and spiritual person," the statement said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Once he makes a decision, he commits to it fully and he was so excited to be visiting Mount Kailash.

"We can do nothing but continue hoping for a miracle that Luke, and the others who remain missing, are found alive and well."

Officials were in contact on Tuesday with an Australian in Tibet, after another Australian, Cara Severino, was located safely on the weekend.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said she was "incredibly thankful" a second Australian has been found, whose identity the government did not confirm.

"It’s hard to imagine the sense of relief their loved ones must be feeling after what will have been an incredibly harrowing few days," Wong said in a statement.

"Despite this second piece of welcome news in recent days, we must remain realistic about the days ahead .... the conditions facing search and recovery teams are extremely challenging."

Nepal's disaster agency said 987 deaths had been counted there, while Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths in their most recent update on Sunday.

Rescuers are racing to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites that were buried in mud by the flooding.

A private-sector association representing power companies said at least 900 workers were unaccounted for at 12 hydropower projects damaged by the flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

At least one expert said that some workers could have access to oxygen, but others warned that the chances of finding survivors were diminishing.

As the rescue efforts intensified, four bodies were recovered from three mud-filled tunnels, Nepal's army said.

Some workers managed to call for help when the disaster struck last Wednesday, and others who managed to flee reported to authorities and relatives that many of their colleagues were still in the tunnels, said Mohan Kumar Dangi, president of the Independent Power Producers' Association.

It was unclear whether rescuers have had any contact with the trapped...
body.zh: 随着死亡人数不断攀升，以及越来越绝望的家庭寻找失踪亲人，救援人员正在竞相营救数百名据信被困在水电站隧道中的工人，这些工人因尼泊尔和中国边境的灾难性洪水而被埋在泥土中。 尼泊尔和中国的死亡人数合计超过 950 人，超过 4400 人失踪，其中包括 43 名澳大利亚人。 代表电力公司的私营部门协会表示，尼泊尔拉苏瓦和努瓦科特地区因山洪爆发而受损的 12 个水电项目中，至少有 900 名工人下落不明。 至少一位专家表示，一些工人可以获得氧气，但其他专家警告说，找到幸存者的机会正在减少。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 尼泊尔军方表示，随着救援工作的加强，从三个充满泥浆的隧道中找到了四具尸体。 独立电力生产商协会主席莫汉·库马尔·丹吉(Mohan Kumar Dangi)表示，上周三灾难发生时，一些工人设法寻求帮助，其他设法逃离的工人向当局和亲属报告，他们的许多同事仍在隧道里。 目前还不清楚自最初发出求救信号以来，救援人员是否与被困工人有过任何接触。 丹吉说，灾难发生六天后，人们越来越担心有些人可能会窒息而死。 救援工作的重点是被困在为控制水流而建造的巨大隧道中的人们。 “这些隧道足够大，可以让卡车通过，”位于孟加拉国达卡的奥地利格拉茨大学的地球科学家雅各布·施泰纳说。 “据我们了解，他们已经设法为一些被困在里面的人提供氧气，并正在努力营救他们。不过，这是一场时间竞赛，因为人们需要食物和水。” Dangi 说，在受灾最严重的 Rasuwa 地区的 Upper Trishuli-1 水电站项目中，至少有 576 人失踪，并补充说，其中约 300 人据信被困在该项目的隧道内。 尼泊尔陆军发言人 Raja Ram Basnet 准将表示，在 Trishuli-3 水电项目中，工作人员正在努力下潜到隧道内约 15 米处，以营救被困在隧道内的人员。 尼泊尔达丁一座遭受洪水破坏的发电站的工人们正在铲泥，他们表示，该发电站是为该地区 2 万多人提供电力的关键线路。 中方的救援和恢复工作包括重建通往吉隆口岸的道路，该口岸负责控制中尼之间的交通。 当工人们试图重新铺设道路时，卡车运载着巨大的岩石。

reflection.en: The news from the Nepal-China border is grim, with hundreds of workers trapped in tunnels following catastrophic floods. In such moments, the cry of the vulnerable echoes, reminding us of the biblical call to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves. May we be moved to advocate for the safety and rescue of these individuals, reflecting the compassion...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔-中国边境传来的消息令人心痛，数百名工人在灾难性的洪水后被困于隧道之中。在这样的时刻，弱者的呼喊回响，提醒我们圣经呼召我们要为那些无法为自己发声的人说话。愿我们被触动，为这些人的安全和救援而倡导，体现《箴言》31:8-9所敦促我们的怜悯之心。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: How China buried Tibet flood images after Nepal disaster
title.zh: 中国如何掩埋了尼泊尔灾难后的西藏洪水图像

summary.en: In Tibet, a digital crackdown followed the deadly flood that has devastated communities along the China-Nepal border. Censors erased viral footage while Chinese state media flooded platforms with official content.
summary.zh: 在西藏，一场致命的洪水摧毁了中国和尼泊尔边境的社区，随后出现了数字审查。审查人员删除了病毒式传播的画面，而中国官方媒体则用官方内容充斥了各大平台。

body.en:
In Tibet, a digital crackdown followed the deadly flood that has devastated communities along the China-Nepal border. Censors erased viral footage while Chinese state media flooded platforms with official content.

When a catastrophic flash flood swept through the rugged China-Nepal border on August 26, the physical devastation was immediate.

In Nepal , a black torrent of mud and rock tore through communities, leaving hundreds dead and thousands more missing along the borderlands.

But across the frontier in Tibet, an autonomous region of China , the physical disaster was almost instantly followed by a digital one: the rapid, high-tech erasure of the catastrophe's visual evidence.

As survivors tried to upload raw footage of the deluge, China's state-backed information control apparatus swung into action, executing a sophisticated, precision operation to shape the public narrative and bury inconvenient truths.

The contrasting realities — a tragic humanitarian crisis in Nepal and a tightly sanitized, triumphant rescue narrative in China — reveal the evolving mechanics of Beijing's modern censorship machine.

Rather than imposing a blunt, blanket blackout, authorities deployed advanced image-recognition technology and "saturated information" tactics to drown out domestic scrutiny while deflecting diplomatic friction abroad.

In the immediate aftermath of the flood-triggered mudslide, local residents captured dramatic footage of the torrent engulfing Gyirong Port, a critical overland trade hub between China and Nepal.

The most striking video showed a black wall of water and debris crashing into and destroying the "national" border gate.

In an article titled "An Unrecorded Mudslide Rushes into Gyirong Port" on China's WeChat, a universal app that combines messaging with payment options and social media functions, local blogger "Matou Qingnian" described the chaotic scene.

"The most terrifying moment happened at the Gyirong Port," the author wrote, describing video footage of crowds, including children, fleeing in panic before a pitch-black torrent swallowed the camera's view.

Within hours, both the article and the raw video footage had vanished from Chinese social media .

According to  China Digital Times (CDT) , an independent watchdog that tracks Chinese internet censorship , the video of the collapsing border gate was systematically blocked from being shared on WeChat, even in private messages.

"The footage itself contained no graphic violence, no protests, and no political slogans," explained Mira, a CDT editor who specializes in tracking sensitive keywords and media. "The target of the censorship was the symbol itself: the National Gate."

Digital analysts note that this censorship highlights a significant upgrade...
body.zh: 在西藏，致命的洪水摧毁了中尼边境沿线的社区，随后进行了数字镇压。审查机构删除了病毒式传播的视频，而中国官方媒体则在平台上充斥着官方内容。 8 月 26 日，一场灾难性的山洪席卷崎岖的中尼边境，造成了立即的破坏。 在尼泊尔，一股黑色泥浆和岩石洪流席卷了边境地区的社区，造成数百人死亡、数千人失踪。 但在中国西藏自治区的边境地区，这场物理灾难几乎立刻就发生了一场数字灾难：灾难的视觉证据被迅速、高科技删除。 当幸存者试图上传洪水的原始镜头时，中国国家支持的信息控制机构立即采取行动，执行复杂而精确的操作，以塑造公众叙事并掩盖难以忽视的真相。 对比鲜明的现实——尼泊尔悲惨的人道主义危机和中国严密消毒、胜利的救援故事——揭示了北京现代审查机制不断演变的机制。 当局没有实施生硬、全面的封锁，而是采用了先进的图像识别技术和“饱和信息”策略来淹没国内审查，同时转移国外的外交摩擦。 洪水引发的泥石流发生后，当地居民拍下了洪流吞没吉隆港的戏剧性镜头，吉隆港是中国和尼泊尔之间重要的陆路贸易枢纽。 最引人注目的视频显示，黑色的水墙和碎片冲撞并摧毁了“国家”边境大门。 当地博主“马头青年”在中国微信（一款将消息传递、支付选项和社交媒体功能结合在一起的通用应用程序）上发表了一篇题为“一场未记录的泥石流冲进吉隆口岸”的文章，描述了当时的混乱场面。 “最可怕的时刻发生在吉隆口岸，”作者写道，并描述了包括儿童在内的人群在漆黑的洪流吞没摄像机视野之前惊慌失措的画面。 几个小时内，这篇文章和原始视频片段就从中国社交媒体上消失了。 据追踪中国互联网审查制度的独立监管机构中国数字时代（CDT）称，倒塌边境大门的视频被系统性地禁止在微信上分享，甚至在私人信息中也是如此。 专门跟踪敏感关键词和媒体的 CDT 编辑米拉解释说：“视频本身不包含暴力画面、抗议活动和政治口号。” “审查的目标是标志本身：国门。” 数字分析师指出，这次审查凸显了重大升级......

reflection.en: The story describes how visual evidence of a devastating flood in Tibet was systematically erased, replaced by official narratives. This act of censorship raises questions about truth and transparency, reminding us of the importance of speaking truthfully and avoiding deception, as Ephesians 4:25 urges.
reflection.zh: 故事描述了西藏一场毁灭性洪水的视觉证据如何被系统性地抹去，并被官方叙事所取代。这种审查行为引发了关于真相和透明度的疑问，提醒我们说实话和避免欺骗的重要性，正如以弗所书4:25所敦促的那样。

verse.textEn: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbor.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要弃绝谎言，各人与邻舍说实话。

title.en: Why China is censoring footage of the Nepal-Tibet disaster
title.zh: 中国为何审查尼泊尔-西藏灾难的视频

summary.en: A catastrophic flood event in Tibet has been met with apparent censorship by Chinese authorities, with footage of the disaster conspicuously absent from domestic media. This highlights the extreme sensitivity and tight control China exerts over information from Tibet, a region with a long and contested history.
summary.zh: 在西藏发生的一场灾难性洪水事件中，中国当局似乎进行了审查，相关视频在中国国内媒体上明显缺失。这凸显了中国对其拥有长期且备受争议历史的西藏地区信息实施的极端敏感性和严密控制。

body.en:
A natural disaster may not seem inherently political. But in Tibet, even footage of a flood can be sensitive.

As videos circulated widely on social media and in news reports last week, showing a devastating torrent of mud, water and debris tearing through a border post between Tibet and Nepal, correspondents in Beijing began to point out a striking absence: in China, the footage was nowhere to be seen.

The apparent censorship highlights the extraordinary sensitivity surrounding Tibet, one of the most tightly controlled regions under Chinese control, and the long and highly contested history stretching back hundreds of years.

Tsering Yangzom, a member of the Tibetan community in Newcastle, NSW, told SBS News her uncle works in the flood-affected region of Tibet, but she's been unable to contact him since the disaster and appears to have been blocked.

She suspects he may be concerned their communications are being monitored, but she's also "really, really worried" about whether he was affected by the deadly floods.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Normally, she says they speak briefly and intermittently on the Chinese messaging app WeChat, sometimes using coded language to protect her uncle.

"If he says the weather is good, then we can talk a little bit more about the normal life," said Yangzom, who says she changed her name after leaving left Tibet as a child.

"But if he says the weather is not good and rainy or something ... that means that I can't talk much."

Human Rights Watch's Australia director, Daniela Gavshon, told SBS News censorship and self-censorship are pervasive in Tibetan areas.

"These information controls make it even harder to get accurate information, for families to locate loved ones, or to develop a good understanding of the disaster, its scale, its impact, and the response."

Tibet, isolated both geographically and diplomatically, sits atop a vast area of mountains and plateaus and is often referred to as the "roof of the world".

For centuries, it has had a complicated relationship with China. Beijing maintains that Tibet has been part of China since ancient times, while Tibetans say it had long been independent with its own unique culture, religion and language.

In 1950, troops from China's newly established communist government invaded Tibet and defeated Tibetan forces, in a move the Chinese government described as part of the "peaceful liberation" of the region.

The following year, Tibetan representatives signed an agreement recognising Chinese sovereignty over Tibet, while promising the region autonomy. Tibetan leaders say they were forced into this agreement.

Tensions over Chinese rule grew in the following...
body.zh: 自然灾害似乎本质上并不具有政治性。但在西藏，即使是洪水的镜头也可能很敏感。 上周，视频在社交媒体和新闻报道中广泛传播，视频显示泥浆、水和碎片席卷了西藏和尼泊尔之间的边境哨所，造成毁灭性的洪流，北京的记者开始指出一个惊人的缺席：在中国，这段视频无处可见。 明显的审查制度突显了西藏的非凡敏感性，西藏是中国控制下控制最严格的地区之一，而且其历史可以追溯到数百年前，历史悠久且充满争议。 新南威尔士州纽卡斯尔藏族社区成员次仁央宗 (Tsering Yangzom) 告诉 SBS 新闻，她的叔叔在西藏受洪水影响的地区工作，但自灾难发生以来，她一直无法联系到他，而且似乎已被封锁。 她怀疑他可能担心他们的通讯受到监控，但她也“非常非常担心”他是否受到致命洪水的影响。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 她说，通常情况下，他们会在中国通讯应用微信上断断续续地简短交谈，有时会使用密码语言来保护她的叔叔。 “如果他说天气好，那么我们就可以多谈谈正常生活，”央宗说。她说，她小时候离开西藏后就改了名字。 “但如果他说天气不好，下雨什么的……那就意味着我不能说太多。” 人权观察组织澳大利亚主任丹妮拉·加夫尚 (Daniela Gavshon) 告诉 SBS 新闻，审查和自我审查在藏族地区十分普遍。 “这些信息控制使得家人更难获得准确的信息、找到亲人，或更好地了解灾难、其规模、影响和应对措施。” 西藏地处广阔的山脉和高原之上，在地理和外交上与世隔绝，通常被称为“世界屋脊”。 几个世纪以来，它与中国有着复杂的关系。北京坚称西藏自古以来就是中国的一部分，而藏人则表示西藏早已独立，拥有自己独特的文化、宗教和语言。 1950年，中国新成立的共产党政府的军队入侵西藏并击败了西藏军队，中国政府称此举是该地区“和平解放”的一部分。 次年，西藏代表签署了一项协议，承认中国对西藏拥有主权，同时承诺实行区域自治。西藏领导人表示，他们是被迫签署这项协议的。 接下来，围绕中国统治的紧张局势加剧……

reflection.en: In the face of a devastating flood, information from Tibet is being suppressed, effectively silencing the experiences of those affected. This echoes the call to 'speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves,' reminding us that truth and visibility are vital, especially when disaster strikes.

title.en: Antisemitism royal commission to report later than planned

summary.en: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion has extended its reporting deadline by four days to avoid coinciding with the first anniversary of the Bondi Massacre, a mass shooting that claimed 15 lives. Commissioner Virginia Bell stated the extension was requested to ensure the report does not overshadow...
summary.zh: 反犹太主义和社会凝聚力皇家委员会将其报告截止日期延长了四天，以避免与邦迪大屠杀一周年纪念日发生冲突，该屠杀事件造成 15 人死亡。委员会主席弗吉尼亚·贝尔表示，延长是为了确保报告不会盖过 12 月 14 日（袭击周年纪念日）的庄严悼念活动。

body.en:
The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion has had its deadline extended by four days so that it does not clash with the anniversary of the Bondi Massacre.

The months-long royal commission was slated to hand down its final report on 14 December, the first anniversary of the mass shooting that left 15 people dead. The commission will now report on 18 December.

In a statement, commissioner Virginia Bell AC SC said she requested the extension from the federal government so that her final report did "not overshadow the first anniversary of the Bondi Chanukah attack".

"The 14th of December will be a solemn occasion marked by memorials," the statement said.

"I am aware of concern within the Jewish community that delivery of the report on the anniversary would be a distraction. I welcome this short extension."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Established on 9 January, the royal commission heard evidence from 348 witnesses over 62 days of hearings in Sydney and Melbourne.

Bell is currently preparing her final report, which will examine this evidence alongside more than 20,000 public submissions.

On 26 August, the final day of public hearings, Bell told the commission her focus had been on the lives of ordinary Jewish Australians.

"The Bondi Chanukah attack came after more than two years of a marked increase in antisemitism throughout Australia," she said.

"Laying out the picture of the lived experience of antisemitism is a critical part of any steps to combat that phenomenon."

An interim report was released on 30 April and made 14 recommendations to strengthen counterterrorism responses.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .

title.en: Kids are being dragged down a troubling 'rabbit hole'. What happens if we switch it off?
title.zh: 孩子们正被拖入一个令人不安的“兔子洞”。如果我们关掉它会怎样？

summary.en: A proposal to fundamentally change how Australians experience social media is gaining traction. The idea is to require social media companies to offer users an option to disable algorithms, defaulting instead to a chronological feed of posts from friends and followed accounts. This aims to protect young people from...

body.en:
The manosphere wouldn't disappear from the internet. But what if we took away the rabbit hole?

That's one of the questions posed by consent advocate Chanel Contos to change the way Australians experience social media and protect young people from the harmful effects of misogynistic online content.

Her organisation, Teach Us Consent, has been campaigning for reforms that would require social media companies to offer Australians a feature that opts them out of algorithms, instead giving people the option to see posts from friends and accounts they follow by default.

International researchers posing as boys aged between 16 and 18 were likely to be fed misogynistic content within 23 minutes of signing up to certain social media accounts, highlighting the role recommendation algorithms can play in exposing young men to harmful ideas.

Contos, in a speech to the National Press Club on Wednesday, accused big tech companies of radicalising young men into harmful sexual acts and called for strict reforms.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

She cited research that suggested the manosphere — an online ecosystem of influencers and communities promoting hypermasculine tropes — should be understood as "a business with various actors who share the same commercial infrastructure who have identified male psychology as a market".

Members of the federal government have signalled support for the proposal amid a broader effort to address the rising rate of sexual violence among young people and a troubling spate of recent incidents.

Teachers have also raised concerns that attitudes from the manosphere are surfacing in Australian schools and driving gendered abuse towards them.

As proposed reforms gain increasing prominence, how much of the manosphere's power actually comes from the algorithm — and what could happen if we switched it off?

Experts note that the ideas driving the manosphere are far from new, but algorithms have transformed how widely and easily they reach young men.

"The manosphere was once used to describe fringe online communities. Men largely had to create an account, sign up, and actively participate in these online message and largely text-based forums," Krista Fisher, research fellow at the Movember Institute of Men's Health, told SBS News.

"The way that the manosphere functions and exists in 2026 is so deeply intertwined with recommender systems, and we've seen that in research," she said.

The rabbit hole can begin with seemingly innocuous content about fitness, dating or self-improvement, before recommendation algorithms begin serving them increasingly extreme material about masculinity and gender roles.

verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Who are the Australians missing in the Nepal floods? What we know so far
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水失踪的澳大利亚人是谁？我们目前所知

summary.en: Thirty-eight Australians are among thousands missing following deadly flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border. Rescue efforts are ongoing, and the number of missing Australians has decreased slightly as some individuals have made contact.
summary.zh: 在尼泊尔-西藏边境发生致命的洪水灾害后，有38名澳大利亚人失踪，他们是数千名失踪人员中的一部分。救援工作正在进行中，随着一些失踪人员取得联系，失踪的澳大利亚人数略有下降。

body.en: There are 38 Australians among the thousands of people missing as rescue efforts continue after deadly flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The number of Australians missing in the Nepal-Tibet flash flooding disaster fell from 43 on Tuesday morning to 38 on Wednesday, with five unaccounted for people making contact. Of the five Australians confirmed safe on Wednesday, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet and three outside the crisis-hit area. Continue reading...
body.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏边境发生致命山洪，救援工作仍在继续，数千人失踪，其中有 38 名澳大利亚人失踪 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 尼泊尔-西藏山洪爆发灾难中失踪的澳大利亚人人数从周二上午的 43 人减少到周三的 38 人，其中有 5 人下落不明。周三确认安全的五名澳大利亚人中，一名在尼泊尔被发现，一名在西藏，三名在危机重灾区之外。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In the midst of devastating floods in Nepal, 38 Australians are among the thousands unaccounted for. This situation calls to mind Jesus' words that whatever we do for the least of these, we do for Him. Our prayers are with those missing, their families, and the rescue workers.
reflection.zh: 在尼泊尔毁灭性的洪水灾难中，有38名澳大利亚人失踪，他们是数千名失踪人员中的一员。这一情况让人想起耶稣的话：我们为最小的弟兄所做的，就是为祂做的。我们的祷告与失踪者、他们的家人以及救援人员同在。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: Coalition plan to cut tobacco excise by 80% ‘will kill people,’ Labor says amid public health alarm
title.zh: 联盟党削减烟草消费税80%的计划“会害死人”，工党在公共卫生警报中表示

summary.en: Coalition politicians Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan have proposed an 80% cut to tobacco excise and the legalization of vapes, claiming it will combat the illicit tobacco trade. However, leading public health experts, the Australian Medical Association, and the Labor party have strongly opposed the plan, warning it...

reflection.en: This proposal to drastically cut tobacco taxes, despite warnings from health experts, raises questions about governmental responsibility. Jeremiah 22:3 calls leaders to "execute justice and righteousness, and deliver from the hand of the oppressor him who suffers violence." The debate centers on whether this policy truly serves the public good or risks...
reflection.zh: 这项大幅削减烟草税的提议，尽管有健康专家的警告，引发了关于政府责任的问题。耶利米书22:3呼吁领导人“施行公平和公义，拯救被欺压的脱离欺压者的手。”这场辩论的焦点在于，这项政策是否真正服务于公众利益，还是出于经济或政治原因而可能伤害弱势公民。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.

reflection.en: The raw grief of Tony Ticehurst, confronting his daughter's murderer with a wish for unending torment, speaks to the deep wound left by violence. This cry for justice and remembrance echoes the ancient call to defend the oppressed and plead for the victim, reminding us that true justice seeks not only punishment but also the restoration of dignity for those...

title.en: 'Enormous interest': Coalition says exiled crown prince of Iran will visit Australia
title.zh: “浓厚兴趣”：联盟表示伊朗流亡王储将访问澳大利亚

summary.en: The Coalition says Reza Pahlavi has accepted the party's invitation.
summary.zh: 联盟表示，礼萨·帕拉维已接受该党邀请。

body.en:
Six months after United States President Donald Trump attacked Iran and called for regime change in the country, the Coalition says the exiled crown prince of Iran will visit Australia at their invitation.

Reza Pahlavi is the son of the shah of Iran, who was ousted by the Islamic Revolution. Pahlavi has lived outside Iran since 1979, and has long advocated for the fall of the current regime, positioning himself as an alternative leader for the country.

In a statement, Opposition foreign affairs spokesperson Ted O'Brien said the party's invitation to Pahlavi was not an endorsement of his leadership in Iran.

"Iran's future belongs to the Iranian people. It is not for Australia to determine who should lead Iran or what form its future government should take," O'Brien said.

The statement said the Coalition was "responding to Iranian-Australians who want their voices heard".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"We should be prepared to listen to credible voices advocating for a peaceful and democratic alternative to the regime in Tehran."

The statement said Pahlavi had accepted the Coalition's invitation to visit Australia for the first time since 1978, before his father's regime was overthrown.

The details of this visit are yet to be finalised, but the statement said Coalition MPs and senators would meet "virtually" with the former crown prince in the coming weeks "to discuss the situation in Iran, the aspirations of the Iranian people and his advocacy for a democratic transition to a secular Iran".

In its statement, the Coalition said the invitation had come off the back of "enormous interest from the Iranian-Australian community".

"Thousands of Persian Australians have signed our petition to bring Reza Pahlavi to Australia, Liberal MP Julian Leeser said.

O'Brien said engagement with Iranian-Australians formed part of the Coalition's broader engagement with diaspora communities.

"For decades, the Iranian people have suffered under a brutal terrorist regime that represses its own citizens, exports terror abroad and denies its people basic freedoms."

After entering exile alongside his father Mohammad Reza Pahlavi — the last shah of Iran — Reza Pahlavi has become an avid supporter of opponents to Iran's ayatollahs.

Now living in the US, he has positioned himself as a person who could lead a secular, democratic Iran. He has seen his support soar in Iran and throughout the Iranian diaspora.

In January, domestic demonstrations against the regime gripped Iran, as protesters took to the streets in the thousands to protest the country's economic problems and the regime itself.

The government responded with a communications blackout...
body.zh: 在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普攻击伊朗并呼吁该国政权更迭六个月后，该联盟表示，流亡的伊朗王储将应他们的邀请访问澳大利亚。 礼萨·巴列维（Reza Pahlavi）是被伊斯兰革命推翻的伊朗国王的儿子。巴列维自 1979 年以来一直居住在伊朗境外，长期以来一直主张推翻现政权，将自己定位为该国的替代领导人。 反对党外交事务发言人泰德·奥布莱恩在一份声明中表示，该党邀请巴列维并不意味着支持他在伊朗的领导地位。 奥布莱恩表示：“伊朗的未来属于伊朗人民。谁应该领导伊朗，或者未来的政府应该采取什么形式，这不是由澳大利亚来决定的。” 声明称，该联盟正在“回应那些希望自己的声音被听到的伊朗裔澳大利亚人”。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “我们应该准备好倾听主张以和平、民主的方式取代德黑兰政权的可信声音。” 声明称，巴列维接受了联盟党的邀请，自1978年（其父政权被推翻之前）以来首次访问澳大利亚。 此次访问的细节尚未敲定，但声明称，联盟党议员和参议员将在未来几周内与前王储“虚拟”会面，“讨论伊朗局势、伊朗人民的愿望以及他对向世俗伊朗民主过渡的主张”。 该联盟在声明中表示，这一邀请是出于“伊朗-澳大利亚社区的巨大兴趣”。 自由党议员朱利安·利泽说：“数千名波斯裔澳大利亚人签署了我们的请愿书，将礼萨·巴列维带到澳大利亚。” 奥布莱恩表示，与伊朗裔澳大利亚人的接触是联盟与侨民社区更广泛接触的一部分。 “几十年来，伊朗人民一直遭受残酷的恐怖主义政权的迫害，该政权镇压本国公民，向国外输出恐怖，并剥夺其人民的基本自由。” 在与他的父亲穆罕默德·礼萨·巴列维（伊朗最后一位国王）一起流亡后，礼萨·巴列维已成为伊朗阿亚图拉反对者的狂热支持者。 现在居住在美国，他将自己定位为一个可以领导世俗、民主伊朗的人。他在伊朗和整个伊朗侨民中的支持率飙升。 一月份，伊朗国内爆发了针对该政权的示威活动，数千名抗议者走上街头，抗议该国的经济问题和该政权本身。 政府的回应是通讯中断……

reflection.en: Reza Pahlavi, the exiled heir to Iran's throne, has accepted an invitation to visit Australia. For decades, he has advocated for change in his homeland, positioning himself as a potential alternative leader. This visit brings attention to the ongoing struggles and aspirations of the Iranian people for self-determination.
reflection.zh: 伊朗流亡王储礼萨·帕拉维已接受澳大利亚的访问邀请。数十年来，他一直倡导祖国的变革，并将自己定位为潜在的替代领导人。此次访问将人们的目光引向伊朗人民持续的斗争和对自决的渴望。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: The world is expected to overshoot a critical climate target. But there's still hope
title.zh: 全球预计将突破关键气候目标，但仍存希望

summary.en: A new United Nations report indicates the world will likely surpass 1.5C of warming by 2030. Despite this concerning projection, experts suggest that immediate actions and political will can still mitigate the worst effects and shape a climate-safe future.
summary.zh: 一份新的联合国报告指出，世界可能在2030年前超过1.5摄氏度的升温目标。尽管这一预测令人担忧，但专家们认为，当前的行动和政治意愿仍能减轻最严重的影响，并塑造一个气候安全的未来。

body.en:
That's no longer possible, according to a new United Nations report. We will likely pass 1.5C in 2030. That's not good news for anyone, least of all Australia's Pacific Island neighbours who face rapidly rising seas.

In response to the report, Palau's President Surangel Whipps Jr said: "It is hard to overstate the depth of emotion for those of us living on the front-line after having fought so hard to put the 1.5 degree limit at the heart of the Paris Agreement … calls for greater ambition are no longer enough — we need to see an urgent and unprecedented increase in political will and investment in a climate safe future."

The small silver lining is that it's still possible for this to be a temporary overshoot of the target.

If nations redouble their efforts to phase out fossil fuels and reduce other sources of emissions, they could limit peak warming to 1.8C and then use carbon removal methods to bring temperatures back to 1.5C or below this century.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In 2026, the world is already about 1.4C warmer than pre-industrial levels, and the damage and death toll from climate-boosted disasters is ramping up.

The United Kingdom is warning of possible food shortages amid a historic drought.

Wildfires hit new areas in France and Spain, while glaciers are melting rapidly and the oceans are at their hottest level on record.

The enormous El Niño event emerging in the Pacific is likely to bring major disruption. Every fraction of a degree makes things worse.

There are no good outcomes if we remain above 1.5C. Urgent cuts to emissions and efforts to protect the most vulnerable are our best remaining options. Failure to do so risks irreversible harm.

The 2015 Paris Agreement established a shared goal for the world: keep the rise in global average temperatures above pre-industrial levels "well below" 2C and "pursue efforts" to hold warming to 1.5C.

This goal was set based on expert scientific assessments that warming of more than 2C would be dangerous and that limiting warming to 1.5C was necessary to minimise climate risks.

Pacific nations fought hard to include 1.5C in the agreement, arguing it was essential for their communities to "stay alive" in the face of rising sea levels and other climate-fuelled threats.

Last year, the world's top court — the International Court of Justice — ruled that 1.5C is the primary temperature limit nations have committed to work towards.

This ruling means that if governments fail to act as ambitiously as they can, they could be sued in international courts.

body.zh: 根据联合国的一份新报告，这已不再可能。到 2030 年，气温可能会超过 1.5 摄氏度。这对任何人来说都不是好消息，尤其是面临海平面迅速上升的澳大利亚太平洋岛屿邻国。 帕劳总统小苏兰吉尔·惠普斯在回应这份报告时表示：“我们这些生活在第一线的人们，在为将 1.5 度气温限制纳入《巴黎协定》的核心而进行了艰苦奋斗后，其情感之深怎么形容都不为过……仅仅呼吁更大的雄心已经不够了——我们需要看到政治意愿和投资以前所未有的方式紧迫增加，以实现气候安全的未来。” 一线希望是，这仍然有可能暂时超出目标。 如果各国加倍努力逐步淘汰化石燃料并减少其他排放源，他们可以将峰值升温限制在 1.8 摄氏度，然后使用碳去除方法将本世纪气温恢复到 1.5 摄氏度或以下。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 到 2026 年，世界气温已比工业化前水平高出约 1.4 摄氏度，气候引发的灾难造成的损失和死亡人数正在不断增加。 英国警告称，在历史性干旱期间可能出现粮食短缺。 野火袭击了法国和西班牙的新地区，冰川正在迅速融化，海洋达到有记录以来的最热水平。 太平洋地区出现的巨大厄尔尼诺事件可能会带来重大破坏。每一度的一小部分都会让事情变得更糟。 如果温度保持在 1.5 摄氏度以上，不会有什么好结果。紧急削减排放和努力保护最弱势群体是我们剩下的最佳选择。如果不这样做，可能会造成不可逆转的伤害。 2015年《巴黎协定》为世界确立了一个共同目标：将全球平均气温上升幅度控制在工业化前水平“远低于”2摄氏度，并“努力”将升温控制在1.5摄氏度以内。 这一目标是根据专家科学评估制定的，专家的科学评估认为升温超过 2 摄氏度将是危险的，并且有必要将升温限制在 1.5 摄氏度，以尽量减少气候风险。 太平洋国家为将 1.5℃ 纳入协议进行了艰苦的斗争，认为面对海平面上升和其他气候引发的威胁，它们的社区必须“生存”。 去年，世界最高法院——国际法院——裁定 1.5 摄氏度是各国承诺努力实现的主要温度限制。 这项裁决意味着，如果政府未能尽其所能采取雄心勃勃的行动，他们可能会在国际法庭上被起诉。 今年五月，大多数国家在联合国大会上投票支持了法院的...

title.en: Coalition plan to hit 'gangs where it hurts' would slash tobacco tax and legalise vapes
title.zh: 联盟计划通过削减烟草税和合法化电子烟来打击“黑帮的痛处”

summary.en: The Opposition has unveiled its plan to tackle the sale of illegal tobacco amid the rise of organised crime sales. Tobacco tax would be cut by as much as 80 per cent under a new Coalition plan unveiled on Wednesday, in an effort to reduce the lucrative nature of the illicit market. The plan would also legalise the...
summary.zh: 反对党公布了其打击非法烟草销售的计划，以应对有组织犯罪的销售增长。根据反对党周三公布的一项新计划，烟草税将削减高达80%，以降低非法市场的利润。该计划还将使目前受限制的尼古丁电子烟设备和尼古丁袋合法化。反对党财政发言人蒂姆·威尔逊表示，该计划将增加联邦收入，同时减少流向有组织犯罪的现金。

body.en:
Tobacco tax would be cut by as much as 80 per cent under a new Coalition plan unveiled on Wednesday.

Opposition leader Angus Taylor has outlined his plan to reduce the tax paid on purchases of cigarettes and tobacco products in an effort to reduce the lucrative nature of the illicit market.

The plan would also legalise the sale of nicotine vaping devices and nicotine pouches, which are currently restricted.

Opposition treasury spokesperson Tim Wilson said the plan will increase federal revenue while reducing cash flow to organised crime.

"It'll increase government revenue by about $2 billion a year because it will stop people buying products from the black market and will lead to them buying it in the real market," Wilson told ABC Radio National.

He argued that Labor was too focused on law enforcement while One Nation — who announced their policy of a 75 per cent reduction in tobacco duty — was too focused on cutting tax alone.

"We actually get the outcome Australians want, which is to break illegal tobacco trade, stop fuelling the fire bombings of stores ... and make sure we raise revenue to deliver a better health outcome," he said.

The Coalition has said its 80 per cent reduction plan will be backed by a $200 million nationwide crackdown on the illegal tobacco trade, which it says earns criminal gangs between $4.1 billion and $6.9 billion in profit each year.

A $60 million, three-year "public awareness and education campaign" would also be conducted to warn Australians of the dangers of smoking.

Labor Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino has previously rejected such a plan, arguing there is no evidence to show cutting taxes would eliminate the illegal trade.

Public health authorities have long advocated for raising tobacco duty in an effort to price consumers out of the market. They have consistently warned that cutting taxes will reverse decades of decline in national smoking rates.

Laura Hunter, CEO of the Australian Council on Smoking and Health, previously told SBS News making cigarettes cheaper would have "huge ramifications for the health of Australians".

"Australia now has the lowest smoking rates that we've ever recorded, and that's the result of decades of policies that are designed to make cigarettes less affordable, less available in the community, and less normalised," she said.

However, the Coalition points to Australian Bureau of Statistics figures that show tobacco consumption increased by roughly 30 per cent between 2022 and 2025.

title.en: Missing Australians in Nepal to be pinpointed using telco data
title.zh: “像一家人”：澳大利亚尼泊尔社区焦急等待答案

summary.en: More than a week on from deadly flash floods in Nepal and Tibet, thousands of people remain missing, with 38 Australians unaccounted for and rescuers racing against time.
summary.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏发生致命的洪水灾害已超过一周，仍有数千人失踪，其中38名澳大利亚人下落不明，救援人员争分夺秒。

body.en:
Telecommunication data is being provided to Nepali authorities to help narrow down the last known locations of Australians missing after catastrophic floods.

Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong said concerns deepen every day for the 38 Australians still unaccounted for, as the total death toll surpasses 1200.

Nepali rescue teams are expected to search in locations where many Australians are believed to have been staying, Ms Wong said during a press conference on Thursday.

The dozens of Australians are among 4200 people missing after a glacier collapse near Nepal's border with China triggered devastating floods across towns and valleys.

"I can indicate that after our inquiries that Nepali authorities have advised us that searches are being conducted in the locations identified by Australia, including [The Kailash Hotel] and the Royal Himalaya Hotel amongst others," Ms Wong said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"In both areas, army personnel are conducting searches on foot with helicopter and drone support."

Foreign Minister Penny Wong confirmed on Thursday that a team of specialist drone operators are being deployed to help with the effort.

The 15-person team will include members of state fire and rescue departments and will use advanced technology to provide rapid mapping and imaging.

There remains no change in the number of missing Australians. Six citizens have been confirmed safe since the disaster last Wednesday.

"Australian officials are working closely with authorities in Nepal and China to support efforts to establish their whereabouts and provide assistance to their families," Wong said.

"Communications are difficult, infrastructure has been destroyed and many areas are still difficult to reach."

Aid supplies aboard a Royal Australian Air Force plane arrived in Kathmandu on Wednesday, carrying humanitarian assistance and disaster relief.

More than 1,400 hygiene kits, 2,200 solar lights and phone chargers were among the items on board.

Australians have donated more than $4 million to the Emergency Action Alliance to support recovery efforts.

The federal government will provide an additional $3 million to match public donations, bringing the ongoing humanitarian support package to $11 million.

Grieving community members in Australia continue to cling to hope their loved ones are safe.

"Lots of people are stuck in the tunnels over there as well, and most don't have any contact ... we are still hopeful that maybe we can get good news," Non-Resident Nepali Association Victoria co-ordinator Mahadev Dhanuk told the Australian Associated Press (AAP).

The tight-knit Victorian Nepali community of less than 30,000 is wrapping its...
body.zh: 澳大利亚尼泊尔社区仍然对一周前袭击该国与西藏边境的灾难性洪水中失踪亲人的福祉充满希望。 当地官员担心，许多人被埋在中国边境附近城镇和山谷的洪水留下的废墟下，死亡人数至少达到 1,204 人，仍有 4,200 多人失踪。 外交和贸易部 (DFAT) 周三证实，尽管已确认 5 名公民安全，但仍有 38 名澳大利亚人在洪水影响区失踪，当局对此表示严重关切。 灾难发生一个多星期后，救援人员正在争分夺秒地寻找幸存者，但澳大利亚悲痛的社区成员仍然抱有希望。 “很多人也被困在那边的隧道里，大多数人都没有任何联系……我们仍然希望能得到好消息，”非居民尼泊尔协会维多利亚州协调员马哈德夫·达努克告诉澳大利亚美联社（AAP）。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 作为尼泊尔总理救灾基金的一部分，该协会已通过社区捐款筹集了近 75,000 美元用于该地区的救灾工作。 不到 30,000 人的紧密团结的维多利亚尼泊尔社区正在拥抱那些受悲剧影响的人，周一，数百人在墨尔本举行烛光守夜活动，悼念遇难者。 达努克说：“许多人个人并未受到影响，但从文化上来说，我们感觉就像一个家庭。这就是为什么每个人都感到震惊。” “所有社区都在努力克服自己的困境，并试图提供帮助，并思考我们如何才能与尼泊尔站在一起？” 政府表示，尼泊尔和西藏的官员已确认五名澳大利亚人安全，另外三人则位于危机地区之外。 在阳光海岸，社区成员正在“尽其所能”团结在失踪的残疾支持人员蕾妮·斯普里 (Renee Spry) 的亲人周围。 昆士兰州一位双胞胎女儿的母亲刚刚从尼泊尔-西藏边境附近的一个移民中心的冈仁波齐峰朝圣回来，几分钟后灾难性洪水席卷了该地区。 阳光海岸反对党外交事务发言人泰德·奥布莱恩 (Ted O'Brien) 告诉澳联社：“每次听到有人被发现生还的消息，我们都会感到无比的喜悦和宽慰。” “当然，阳光海岸的我们所有人都会把注意力转向蕾妮，我们满怀希望地想到她的困境。” 另一位失踪的澳大利亚人卢克·科斯坦佐的家人周二发表声明，讲述他们面临的“难以想象的困难局面”。 像斯普瑞一样，...

For the Nepali community in Australia, the wait for news of loved ones is agonizing, a testament to the deep bonds of family and friendship. In times of such sustained loss, we are reminded of Yahweh's enduring mercies, which are new each morning, even amidst the...

title.zh: 澳大利亚人将失去此疫苗的免费使用权。这可能会付出什么代价

summary.en: Some Australians may soon face a new health bill under changes taking effect soon. From 1 October, COVID-19 vaccines will move from the free National COVID-19 Vaccine Program to the routine National Immunisation Program (NIP). While funded vaccination will be targeted at those most at risk, others may need to pay...
summary.zh: 一些澳大利亚人很快将面临新的医疗账单，因为相关变化即将生效。从10月1日起，COVID-19疫苗将从免费的国家COVID-19疫苗计划转为常规的国家免疫计划（NIP）。虽然有资金支持的疫苗接种将针对风险最高的人群，但其他人可能需要自费购买，人们担心费用会成为障碍。

body.en:
Australians who have previously received COVID-19 vaccines for free could soon face an out-of-pocket cost, with experts warning price could become a barrier for some people who still stand to benefit from vaccination.

From 1 October, COVID-19 vaccines will move into the routine National Immunisation Program (NIP), replacing the stand-alone National COVID-19 Vaccine Program established during the pandemic.

Under the new arrangements, funded vaccination will be targeted at people considered most at risk of severe COVID-19, while those outside the eligibility criteria can choose to buy a vaccine privately.

But there is currently no nationally set price for a privately purchased COVID-19 vaccine.

The Department of Health told SBS News in a statement that private vaccine supply and pricing were commercial matters for manufacturers and providers, and that the government did not control private-market prices.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The Pharmacy Guild of Australia also said it was too early to give patients a reliable estimate of the total cost.

"Without knowing the cost of buying the vaccine, it is impossible to provide a reliable indicative total cost to patients," a spokesperson told SBS News.

"Individual pharmacies will set their prices taking into account the cost of purchasing the vaccine and providing the vaccination service."

Royal Australian College of General Practitioners Public Health Special Interest Group chair Dr Peter Markey said he expected privately purchased COVID-19 vaccines could cost between $30 and $80, although he stressed no price had yet been confirmed.

He said the eventual cost would depend on individual pharmacies and encouraged people who wanted a vaccine to compare prices.

"Let's hope it's not going to be too much more than the regular seasonal flu vaccine," Markey said.

The Pharmacy Guild said COVID-19 vaccination would remain a core pharmacy service, with Australia's 6,000 community pharmacies continuing to provide vaccinations.

Professor Julie Leask, professor of Public Health at the University of Sydney's Infectious Diseases Institute, said she supported the COVID-19 vaccine being normalised as part of the routine vaccination schedule.

Her research through Australia's National Vaccine Insights Survey, which surveys more than 2,000 adults each year, found cost was reported as a barrier by about a quarter of people who experienced difficulty getting a flu vaccine.

Leask said an out-of-pocket COVID-19 vaccination could create a practical barrier for people who had to weigh the cost against other household expenses.

title.en: With falls accelerating, how far could Australia's property market drop?
title.zh: 50年低点，还是不是：在澳大利亚房地产市场低迷之际，哪些数字对您最重要？

summary.en: Prices are now falling in most capital-city suburbs, but the key question is how much further the downturn has to run. Australia's property price downturn continues apace, with home values across the nation now 3.6 per cent below their early-2026 peak, according to new figures from property market research firm...
summary.zh: 目前，价格正在大多数首府城市的郊区下跌，但关键问题是这次低迷还会持续多久。根据房地产市场研究公司Cotality的最新数据，澳大利亚的房地产价格下跌仍在继续，全国房价目前比2026年初的峰值低3.6%。出乎意料的急剧下跌促使主要金融机构更新了预测，联邦银行现在预计价格下跌将比该银行此前预测的“更快、更广泛”。房地产价格...

body.en:
Australia's property price downturn continues apace, with home values across the nation now 3.6 per cent below their early-2026 peak, according to new figures from property market research firm Cotality.

A sharper than expected drop has prompted major financial institutions to update their forecasts, with the Commonwealth now expecting "faster and broader" price drops than the bank had previously forecast.

Property prices peaked and began to dip from March of this year, following signals that the federal government planned to remove some tax incentives for property investors .

Interest-rate rises, supply challenges and market sentiment are also thought to have played a part in the recent downturn.

In response to the latest statistics, Housing Minister Claire O'Neil said the nation's property market was "inherently cyclical".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"We see periods of really strong house price growth that are followed by a period of housing downturn — that's happened now about four times in the last decade," she told Channel Seven's Sunrise on Wednesday morning.

The median price of housing in Australia has increased by more than 400 per cent since 1999, according to recent Treasury analysis. O'Neil said that the continuation of this long-term trend would shatter aspirations for future generations.

Whilst one economist says the downturn could be the most significant in 50 years, forecasters differ on how far prices will fall, partly because of differing expectations about important factors such as interest rate changes.

House prices across the nation dropped by 0.9 per cent in August, according to Cotality's national Home Value Index, contributing to a 3.1 per cent fall over the winter quarter.

The drop stretches to 3.6 per cent if measured from when property prices peaked in March of this year.

Cotality also found that 93 per cent of capital city suburbs were now experiencing property price drops. That's more than double the 45.8 per cent of such suburbs that were seeing declines through 2026's autumn months.

Darwin was the only state or territory capital to buck the downward trend, recording a 0.6 per cent increase over the last month and 0.9 per cent over the quarter.

At the other end of the spectrum, prices are falling fastest in Sydney, with home values decreasing by 1.4 per cent in August and 4.7 per cent across the quarter.

The Commonwealth Bank is now expecting prices to fall by around 9 per cent nationwide from a March 2026 peak before bottoming out in April 2027.

body.en:
China and Taiwan's diplomatic tug-of-war is casting a shadow over the ongoing Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) as a handful of national leaders declined to attend — however, experts on the ground caution that a geopolitical focus risks ignoring the core priorities of Australia's neighbours.

The annual 18-member gathering in the Taiwanese-allied nation of Palau opened on Monday with climate change, economic security, and the rising influence of the transnational drug trade top of the agenda.

China has said it has "serious concerns" that Taiwan was invited to attend in its own right, while questions have been raised about whether China has influenced five of 18 national leaders from the forum (those of Kiribati, Fiji, Vanuatu, Samoa and Solomon Island) not to attend.

The cornerstone regional political forum began this year with a pointed message from Palau's President Surangel Whipps Jr, who urged nations to adhere to this year's theme of unity and reminded outside partners that they "do not choose our destination".

This year's PIF takes place as Kiribati moves to constitutionally restrict diplomatic recognition to UN member states only — thus excluding Taiwan — while China actively seeks to strip Taiwan of its 'development partner' status in the forum. This comes nearly two months after a Chinese ballistic missile test in the Pacific Ocean .

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Taiwan, a self-governing democracy, broke away from mainland China in 1949. China views it as Chinese territory that must be brought under its control by force if necessary.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has made strengthening regional ties a key focus of his administration's foreign policy, signing multiple bilateral agreements with countries like Fiji, Vanuatu, and Tuvalu.

But despite the noise around China, "leaders have made it clear they're here to work" Tess Newton Cain, principal consultant at Asia-Pacific strategic firm Sustineo, told SBS News from Koror.

"The issue of the China-Taiwan tussle is largely a distraction, and one that they try to minimise."

On Wednesday, $600 million in Australian funding was announced to tackle transnational drug smuggling from South America that is increasingly causing harm across the Pacific.

China has made the PIF something of a battleground, maintaining that Taiwan ought to be sidelined during talks, as it is not technically a "dialogue partner" due to a difficult compromise that PIF members have reached over its status for the past three decades.

Palau, one of the few nations that maintains official diplomatic ties with Taiwan, has accused China of running a coercion campaign against it after travel...
